sentences.text: Aquilarhinus is a genus of hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur known from the Aguja Formation in Texas, United States.
The only known species in the genus Aquilarhinus is Aquilarhinus palimentus.
Researchers infer that Aquilarhinus possessed a shovel-like beak morphology distinct from other hadrosaurs due to its unusual dentary.
The specific name palimentus refers to the shovel-like shape of the predentary bone, derived from Latin words for shovel and chin.
The holotype specimen of Aquilarhinus was discovered in the Lower Shale of the Aguja Formation within Big Bend National Park, Texas.
Most parts of the Aquilarhinus holotype were collected in 1983, with additional elements found during excavations in 1999.
The species was reclassified into the new genus Aquilarhinus and named Aquilarhinus palimentus in 2019.
The unique rostrum shape of Aquilarhinus is interpreted as an adaptation for shoveling and scooping up vegetation.
Aquilarhinus is classified within the family Hadrosauridae.
Aquilarhinus belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea.
Aquilarhinus is part of the infraorder Iguanodontia.
Aquilarhinus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now North America.
The time range for Aquilarhinus is estimated to be between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian.
